messages:
Hannah M: Pinging the groupwe saw a weird oscillation on dedicated pools last night during a mixed-tenant blast. Not the usual headroom pattern.
Ishaan P: What did the metrics look like? latency or telemetry gaps?
Hannah M: Latency ok, but node churn spiked. Autoscaler issued repeated scale-downs followed by immediate scale-ups. No obvious external traffic pulse.
Joey T: I dug into the operator logs. The scale-down path waits for grace_period, but the grace timer was being reset by stray lease-refresh events. So nodes never satisfied steady state check.
Kim N: Oh that explains it. Lease-refresh from the allocator can come late and look like new load. We need to separate lifecycle signals from telemetry-derived headroom.
Lina Q: Suggestion: introduce a decision tag for each scale intent: {source: telemetry|operator|manual} and only allow operator-originated intents to trigger teardown if telemetry confirms low utilization for N windows.
Ishaan P: +1. Also considering: slow down scale-down by ramp factor. e.g. max_down_rate: 1 node / 30s per pool. That avoids ripple when many nodes eligible.
Joey T: We should add soft-hold for recently-toppled tenants. If a tenant consumed burst credits in last M minutes, don't evict their prewarm immediately. Keeps latency-friendly cases stable.
Hannah M: Good call. Propose combined rule:
```
policy:
  max_down_rate: 1/30s
  scale_down_requirements:
    - util_median(window=20s) < 0.3
    - no_recent_burst_credit_usage: 10m
    - operator_intent_confirmed_by_telemetry: true
```
Kim N: How about local fallback? If controlplane telemetry queueing is delayed, runtime can locally keep N warm replicas for Xs and accept temporary decisions until controlplane syncs. That reduces oscillation from handoff delays.
Ishaan P: That requires trust boundaries. Runtime-local decisions must be conservative and have short ttl. Maybe runtime can request a temporary lease extension token with a nonce so controlplane can reconcile.
Lina Q: We also need observability flags: emit `scale_candidate_reason` and `scale_action_final` so we can correlate operator vs telemetry causes in dashboards.
load-bot: synthetic-load test started against pool 'dedicated-us-west-2/g1' at 1758882155 :rocket:
Joey T: For rollout: staged config with slow down + requirement add, then chaos tests with delayed telemetry (inject 5-20s lag) and with spurious lease refreshes. Watch churn and tail latency.
Hannah M: One more thought: introduce a "stability_probe" metric: when a pool is below utilization but churn rate > threshold, mark it degraded and block aggressive sdowns for 5m while we investigate. Helps automated rollbacks.
Ishaan P: That would also help the autoscaler circuit-breaker. If stability_probe trips, switch to conservative policy until manual ack.
Kim N: Will draft small RFC for: (1) decision_tagging (2) max_down_rate (3) runtime temporary-lease token prototype (4) stability_probe metric.
Lina Q: Add a metrics KPIs doc: target churn < 5% per 5m, sdown_count per hour < 2 for healthy pools.
Joey T: If everyone ok, I'll stage the config and run the synthetic tests now.
Hannah M: Go for it. Post results in this thread. Thanks! :thumbsup:
